standard.name: VIGIL Failure Taxonomy
standard.description: Prototype portable classification standard for recurring AI governance failure mechanisms.

family.name: Value Appropriation Integrity Failures
family.plain_english: An actor uses asymmetric access, capability, position, or resources to capture disproportionate value from another contributor's work without an adequate basis for taking or retaining that value.
family.definition: Failures in which asymmetric access, capability, institutional position, stewardship, infrastructure, compute, capital, aggregation capacity, or other structural advantage is used to identify, extract, accelerate, operationalise, commercialise, or otherwise capture intellectual, creative, informational, research, or economic value originating materially from another contributor without proportionate consent, attribution, compensation, participation, benefit sharing, or another independently adequate basis for the appropriation.
family.invariant: Access does not confer entitlement to appropriate value. Public availability does not by itself extinguish contributor interests. Structural capability, compute, capital, institutional position, or technical ability must not be treated as sufficient ethical authority to capture disproportionate value from another contributor's work.
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is disproportionate capture of another contributor's intellectual, creative, informational, research, or economic value enabled or materially amplified by asymmetric access, capability, institutional position, stewardship, infrastructure, compute, capital, aggregation capacity, or comparable structural advantage.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because one actor benefits from publicly available information, learns from another person's work, independently develops a similar result, competes successfully, cites prior work, or lawfully reuses material. A qualifying event requires evidence that another contributor's value-producing work materially contributed to the captured value and that structural advantage was used to appropriate or disproportionately capture that value without an adequate basis such as meaningful consent, proportionate attribution, compensation, participation, benefit sharing, or equivalent entitlement.

classes.name: Privileged-Access Appropriation
classes.plain_english: An actor uses privileged or structurally advantaged access to another contributor's work, together with superior capability or resources, to capture value that materially depends on that contribution without proportionate participation in the resulting benefit.
classes.definition: A failure in which an actor obtains privileged or structurally advantaged visibility of another contributor's intellectual work, reasoning, data, research, creative contribution, technical artefacts, or value-producing activity and uses that informational advantage, together with materially superior compute, capital, institutional capacity, aggregation capability, distribution, or other resources, to identify, accelerate, operationalise, commercialise, pre-empt, or otherwise capture resulting value without an independently adequate basis for doing so and without proportionate consent, attribution, compensation, participation, benefit sharing, or equivalent recognition of the originating contribution.

required_conditions: Another contributor has produced intellectual, creative, informational, research, technical, or other value-producing work.
The acting party has privileged or structurally advantaged visibility, access, aggregation capacity, or discoverability relative to that work or its development.

The acting party uses that informational advantage together with materially greater capability, compute, capital, institutional capacity, distribution, or comparable resources to identify, accelerate, operationalise, commercialise, pre-empt, or capture value materially dependent on the contributor's work.

The resulting value capture is disproportionate to the originating contributor's participation and lacks an independently adequate basis such as meaningful consent, proportionate attribution, compensation, participation, benefit sharing, or equivalent entitlement.

exclusions: Independent development where the other contributor's work did not materially inform, enable, accelerate, or direct the captured result.

Ordinary learning, commentary, citation, interoperability, research comparison, or transformative reuse where contributor interests and applicable attribution, consent, licensing, compensation, or benefit-sharing obligations are adequately respected.

Public availability of the source material alone does not establish or exclude this class; public accessibility must not be treated as equivalent to unrestricted ethical entitlement to appropriate resulting value.

A conventional contractual or licensing arrangement that clearly establishes the relevant right to use and capture value and provides the contributor the participation, attribution, compensation, or consideration required by that arrangement.
A pure authority-boundary failure in which access is mistaken for permission to act but no material appropriation or disproportionate capture of another contributor's value occurs.
Ordinary competitive advantage arising from greater resources where another contributor's work was not materially used as an input to identifying, accelerating, or capturing the value.
examples: A platform provider identifies a promising research direction through structurally advantaged access to user work and deploys substantially greater compute and institutional resources to complete or commercialise the result before the originating researcher without proportionate participation in the resulting value.

An organisation systematically identifies high-value open-source contributions, uses privileged ecosystem visibility and superior resources to operationalise them into a competing commercial capability, and captures the resulting value while providing no proportionate attribution, participation, compensation, or benefit sharing to the contributors whose work materially enabled the capability.

relationships.note: Capability-Authority Conflation concerns treating ability or access as permission to act. Privileged-Access Appropriation additionally requires material capture of value originating from another contributor through asymmetric informational and capability advantage.

Secondary-Purpose Authority Transposition may occur where access granted for one purpose is reused for another. Privileged-Access Appropriation is independently defined by disproportionate capture of contributor-originated value.

Objective-Pathway Authority Dominance may explain why an actor pursues an advantageous pathway despite unresolved authority or admissibility. Privileged-Access Appropriation concerns the distinct downstream capture of value originating materially from another contributor.
